**Directions: The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.**

Not get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Not get**' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the adverb 'Not' at the beginning of the sentence is incorrect.
 
• The adverb 'not' is used to **form the negative with **the verbs be, do** and have** (auxiliary verb) and with verbs such as **can, must, will**, etc. (modal verbs).
 
• The word ''**Don't**'' should be used **in place of 'not'**.
 
• ''**Don't**'' is a **negative of the verb 'do'** that means **do not**. It is used **to order or suggest or command or advise not to do something**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: ***Don't get** into the car; it has not been cleaned inside*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Not** is simply used to show negation.

 
 
• **Example:** *It is **not** beautiful*. — here it's used to just show that something is the opposite of beautiful.
 
 
 
• **Don't** is used to order or suggest or command or advise to not to do something.
 
 
• **Example:** ***Don't** close the door*. — here it is ordered or told not to close the door. To not do an action ''don't'' is used.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• दिए गए वाक्य में adverb 'not' का प्रयोग गलत है।
 
• Adverb 'not' का उपयोग **क्रियाओं के साथ नकारात्मक बनाने के लिए** किया जाता है be, do और have (सहायक क्रिया) और क्रियाओं जैसे कि can, must, will, आदि (मोडल क्रिया)।
 
• 'Not' के स्थान पर ''Don't'' शब्द का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
 
• ''Don't'', क्रिया 'do' का negative है जिसका अर्थ है **न करना**। इसका उपयोग **आदेश देने या सुझाव देने या कुछ न करने की सलाह देने के लिए **किया जाता है।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

सही वाक्य: *Don't get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside*.

**Directions: The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.**

The school usually starts at 8 a.m. and is closing at 3 p.m.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**is closing at 3 p.m.**' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the present continuous tense 'is closing **at 3 p.m**' is incorrect.
 
• We use the **present continuous** to talk about **actions that are happening at the present moment but will soon finish**.
 
 
• The **present continuous tense**: **to be (am, is, are) + verb (the present participle)**
 
 
 
• The given sentence is talking about a general routine of opening and closing times of the school.
 
• We use the **present simple tense** when we want to talk about **fixed habits or routines – things that don't change**.
 
 
• The **simple present tense** is formed by using **the root form or by adding ‑s or ‑es to the end**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the **present simple tense ''closes at 3 p.m''** should be used **in place of** the **present continuous tense ''is closing **at 3 p.m**''**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *The school usually starts at 8 a.m. and **closes at 3 p.m***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• दिए गए वाक्य में, present continuous tense 'is closing at 3 p.m' गलत है।
 
• हम present continuous का उपयोग **उन कार्यों के बारे में** बात करने के लिए करते हैं **जो वर्तमान क्षण में हो रहे हैं लेकिन जल्द ही समाप्त हो जाएंगे**।
 
 
• Present continuous tense: to be (am, is, are) + verb (the present participle)
 
 
 
• दिया गया वाक्य **स्कूल के खुलने और बंद होने के समय की सामान्य दिनचर्या के बारे में बात कर रहा है**।
 
• हम present simple tense का उपयोग तब करते हैं **जब हम निश्चित आदतों या दिनचर्या के बारे में **बात करना चाहते हैं - ऐसी चीजें जो नहीं बदलती हैं।
 
 
• Simple present tense मूल रूप का उपयोग करके या अंत में s या ‑es जोड़कर बनता है।
 
 
 
• इसलिए, present continuous tense ''is closing at 3 p.m'' के स्थान पर present simple tense ''closes at 3 p.m'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

सही वाक्य: *The school usually starts at 8 a.m. and closes at 3 p.m*.

• Therefore, the phrase ''**No sooner did I**'' should be used in place of the phrase 'Just when'.

questions.question: A boy walked along two adjacent sides of a rectangular field. If he had walked along the diagonal, then he would have saved a distance equal to one-fourth of the larger side. The ratio of the smaller to the larger side is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A rectangular field with Length, breadth and diagonal. 

**Formula used:**

Pythagoras Theorem

Base² + Perpendicular² = Hypotenuse²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43e342a723233fd683222e4ffe34eabf532362caea6d78de250947e60e0494f3.png] 

Let the Length of the rectangular field = l

⇒ Breadth of the field = b

⇒ Diagonal of the field = d 

Letting that l > b

In triangle right-angle triangle ABC. By using Pythagoras Theorem we have:

l² + b² = d² ......(1)

l + b - d = 1/4 × l 

⇒ l + b - l/4 = d

⇒ 3l/4 + b = d .....(2)

Putting the value of d in equation (1), we get:

l2 + b2 = ( 3l/4 + b)²

⇒ l2 + b2 = 9l²/16 + b² + 2 × 3l/4 × b 

⇒ l2 - 9l2/16 = 3lb/2 

⇒7l/8 = 3b 

⇒ l/b = 3 × 8/7

⇒ b/l = 7/24

**∴ The required ratio between the smaller side and the larger side is 7 : 24.**

questions.question: In a class of 80 students, 60% are girls and the rest are boys. The average weight of boys is 5% more than that of girls. If the average weight of all the students is 51 kg, then what is the average weight (in kg) of the girls?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Girls : Boys = 60% : 40% = 3 : 2.

Let Average weight of Girls = 20 units, then Boys = 21 units (5% more than 20).

Total Weighted Average = [(3 × 20) + (2 × 21)] ÷ 5 = 102 ÷ 5 = 20.4 units.

20.4 units = 51 kg ⇒ 1 unit = 2.5 kg.

Average weight of Girls = 20 units × 2.5 = 50 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total students = 80, Girls = 60%, Average of all = 51 kg, Boys avg = 5% more than girls.

**Formula Used:** Weighted Average = (n₁ × x₁ + n₂ × x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 
• Girls (3 Parts) Weight: x Boys (2 Parts) Weight: 1.05x 
 Mean = 51 kg Weighted Average Representation 

⇒ Number of Girls = 60% of 80 = 48; Number of Boys = 40% of 80 = 32.

⇒ Ratio of Girls : Boys = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

⇒ Let average weight of girls = x kg.

⇒ Average weight of boys = x + 5% of x = 1.05x kg.

⇒ Total Average = (3 × x + 2 × 1.05x) ÷ (3 + 2)

⇒ 51 = (3x + 2.1x) ÷ 5

⇒ 51 × 5 = 5.1x

⇒ 255 = 5.1x

⇒ x = 255 ÷ 5.1 = 50 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• Essentially, an ecosystem is a chain of interactions amongst organisms and their respective environments.

• Ecosystems can be broadly classified into 2 types namely **Terrestrial Ecosystem** and **Aquatic Ecosystem. **

The Terrestrial Ecosystems can be further divided into Forest, Grassland, Tundra, and Desert Ecosystems respectively.

__
 
• **Forest Ecosystem__:- **This type of ecosystem consists of several plants, animals, and microorganisms that live in coordination with the abiotic factors of the environment.​​​
 
• **__Grassland Ecosystem__:- ** The grassland ecosystem mainly consists of grasses and herbs. For example- Temperate grasslands, Savanna grasslands etc.
 
• **__Tundra Ecosystem__:- **Tundra ecosystems lack trees and they are found in a cold climate or in areas of very low rainfall. These are covered with snow for most of the year. For example- Arctic or mountain tops is tundra type of ecosystem.
 
• **__Desert Ecosystem__:- **These are the regions with very little or no rainfall characterized by very hot days and cold nights. For Example- Sahara Desert, Thar Desert, etc.

__

• **__Freshwater Ecosystem__:- **The freshwater ecosystem is an aquatic ecosystem that comprises lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, along with the different wetlands. These type of ecosystems consists of no salt, unlike the marine ecosystems.

questions.question: Which of the following best represents the concept of Net Domestic Product (NDP)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net domestic product (NDP)** is an annual measure of the **economic output of a nation that is adjusted as per the depreciation effect.**
 
• The** NDP** is calculated by **subtracting depreciation from the gross domestic product (GDP).**
 
• An **increased NDP indicates growth in economic health**, while a **decrease would indicate a slowdown of the economy of the country.**
 
• **Depreciation** is the** measure of the decreased monetary value of an asset** over time due to **use, wear and tear, or obsolescence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **__Gross National Income (GNI)__**

__
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI)** is the** total amount of money earned by a nation's people and businesses.**
 
• It is used to measure and track a nation's wealth from year to year.
 
• The number is calculated using the** nation's gross domestic product (GDP) plus the income it receives from abroad.**
 
• India GNI per capita for 2020 was $1,900.

**Net National Product (NNP)__**

 
• **Net national product (NNP) **is the monetary** value of finished goods and services** produced by a country's citizens, overseas and domestically, in a given period.
 
• It is the equivalent of the **Gross National Product (GNP), the total value of a nation's annual output, minus the depreciation.**
 
• NNP is often examined on an **annual basis** as a way to measure a nation's success.

• The Constitution was drafted by the **Constituent Assembly** which comprised of the indirectly elected members along with the nominated members.
 
• The Original Constitution in the** English language **was written by **Prem Bihari Narain Raizada**
 
• The Consitution in **Hindi **was written by another calligrapher **Vasant Krishna Vaidya.**
 
• **Raizada** was **born** in a family of calligraphers in the** year 1901 and he died in the year 1966.**
 
• **Raizada** **did not charge a single penny for writing the Constitution** instead, he wrote his name along with his grandfather's name at the bottom of every page of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**About the Constitution of India:**__

 
• The** Constitution at the time of its inception consisted** of **395 articles, 22 parts, and 8 Schedules.**
 
• At present, this document consists of about** 448 articles, 25 parts and 12 schedules.**
 
• There have been **105 amendments** in the Constitution of India **up to October 2021.**
 
• The** first amendment** was done in** 1951.**
 
• This is the beauty of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Constituent Assembly took almost **2years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete the task of** drafting this historic document.**
 
• There were a total of **11 sessions of the Constituent Assembly during this period.**

questions.question: Kaveri Sankramana is a festival celebrated in ________ in the month of October.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Karnataka.__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kaveri Sankramana** is celebrated in the month **of October.**
 
• This festival marks the **birth of the River Kaveri which originates at Talakaveri in Kodagu.**
 
• During this period, there is a precise moment when the** Sun enters the Libra Zodiac sign (Tula Raashi),** and simultaneously, the holy water springs called the **"tirtha" flows from the kundike (pond) and empties itself into the larger holy tank located at Talakaveri.**
 
• 
 
People immerse themselves in this water as they consider it to be of significant importance.

 
 
• 
 
This holy water, **known as tirtha,** is also collected in bottles and distributed among every Kodava household.

 
 
• 
 
This water is fed to the dying in the belief that they will attain** Moksha (salvation).**

 
 
• 
 
On the next day, another ritual called** Kani Puja** (worshipping mother earth) is performed.

 
 
• 
 
**Kani is considered to be the avatar of Goddess Parvati**, of which,** Goddess Kaveri** is an **incarnation.**

 
 
• 
 
Married women drape themselves in lovely silk sarees and perform rituals which include a taliyatakki bolca (an oil lamp placed on top of rice grains spread on a bell-metal plate), a vegetable wrapped in a red silk- believed to be a symbol of Goddess Kaveri, and adorned with jewelry and flowers, three betel leaves, and three areca nuts are placed on a plate.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Cauvery River (Kaveri) **originates from **Talakaveri **on the Brahmagiri range near **Cherangala village of Kodagu (Coorg) district of Karnataka.**
 
• **The total length of the river- **approximately 800 km.
 
• This holy river flows in the **south-east for 705 km** in the states of **Karnataka and Tamil Nadu**, descends the Eastern Ghats in a series of great falls.

 and then finally empties into the Bay of Bengal south of Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu after breaking into a large number of distributaries forming the delta which is often called the** “garden of southern India”.**
 
• **Total Drainage Area-** 81 thousand Sq.km.
 
• Physiographically, the basin of Kaveri can be segregated into three parts – **the Westen Ghats, the Plateau of Mysore, and the Delta.**
 
• The delta area is the **most fertile tract** in the basin.
 
• **Soil types found in the basin-** **black soils, red soils, laterites, alluvial soils, forest soils, and mixed soils**.
 
• The Karnataka section of the basin receives rainfall mainly from the S-W Monsoon and partially from N-E Monsoon while The section of the basin in Tamil Nadu receives from the North-East Monsoon.
 
• The famous **Sivasamudram Falls **are also located on the river Kaveri.
 
• **Left Bank tributaries of the River**- Harangi, the Hemavati, the Shimsha, and the Arkavati.
 
• **Right Bank tributaries of the River**: Lakshmantirtha, the Kabbani, the Suvarnavati, the Bhavani, the Noyil, and Amaravati.

• He was the son of Bhattiya.
 
• He ruled approximately from **558 BC to 491 BC.**
 
• He was the** contemporary of Gautam Buddha **and also considered as the admirer of the Mahavira.
 
• He made his** capital at Rajgriha/Girivraja (Bihar)** as it was** surrounded by 5 hills** during that time. This made Rajgriha practically impregnable.
 
• He was the **first king who expanded his empire by the use of matrimonial alliances** by marrying **Kosaladevi(princess of Kosala and sister of Presanjit), Chellana (daughter of Licchavi prince of Vaishali), and Khema (princess of Madra, Punjab).**
 
• He was the** first king to have a Standing Army.**
 
• He was initially, **a rival of Avanti king Pradyota, but later did friendship with him** and also, he sent his **royal physician Jivaka to Ujjain**, when Pradyota got infected with jaundice.
 
• He was imprisoned and eventually killed by his son **Ajatshatru.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of a leaf?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Petiole.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leaves are the parts of a plant that absorb sunlight which is vital for the process of photosynthesis.
 
• 
 
Leaves have two main parts: The leaf blade and the Stalk or the petiole

 
 
• 
 
The leaf blade__: It is also called the lamina and is usually broad and flat. It is in this layer that photosynthesis occurs.

 
 
• 
 
It contains a prominent midrib at the center of the leaf blade which is the main vein. From this midrib arise branches called veins.

 
 
• 
 
They are of different types depending upon the type of edges, the pattern of the veins, and the number of blades per leaf.

 
 
• 
 
 __The Petiole__: It is the stalk-like structure in the leaf that forms the link between the leaf blade to the stem. It has tiny tubes, that connect the veins on the leaf blade to the stem. Some of these veins facilitate the transport of water to the leaf while other one carries the food away from the leaf to other parts of the plant.

 
 
• 
 
Some plants also contain another part called__ Stipules __which are small flap-like structures that grow at the base of the petioles in order to protect the petioles when they are growing.

questions.question: Who established the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON)?
questions.solution:

• The **International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), or the Hare Krishna movement,** was founded b His Divine Grace Acharya **Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda in New York City in the year 1966.**
 
• This Society includes major centers, temples, and rural communities, nearly one hundred affiliated vegetarian restaurants, thousands of local meeting groups (**namahattas**), a wide variety of community projects, and millions of congregational members worldwide.
 
• **ISKCON** belongs to the** Gaudiya-Vaishnava sampradaya, **a monotheistic tradition within the Vedic or Hindu culture.
 
• Philosophically it is based on the Sanskrit texts** Bhagavad-Gita and the Bhagavat Purana, or Srimad Bhagavatam.**
 
• These are the historic texts of the devotional bhakti yoga tradition, which teaches that the ultimate goal for all living beings is to reawaken their love for God, or Lord Krishna, the “all-attractive one”.
 
• ISKCON devotees chant God’s names in the form of the maha-mantra, or the great prayer for deliverance:** "Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare/Hare Rama Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare".**
 
• 
 
Members of **ISKCON practice bhakti-yoga** in their homes and also worship in temples.

 
 
• 
 
They also promote **bhakti-yoga, or Krishna Consciousness, through festivals, **the performing arts, yoga seminars, public chanting, and the distribution of the society’s pieces of literature.

 
 
• 
 
**ISKCON** members have also opened hospitals, schools, colleges, eco-villages, free food distribution projects, and other institutions as a practical application of the path of devotional yoga.

questions.question: As per Newlands’ Octaves, which of the following has the same properties as sodium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Lithium.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1866, John Newlands, **an** English scientist**, arranged the then-known elements in the **order of increasing atomic masses.**
 
• He started with the element having **the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen)** and **ended at thorium which was the 56th element.**
 
• He found that** every eighth element **had properties similar to that of the first. He compared this to the** octaves found in music.**
 
• Therefore, he called it the** ‘Law of Octaves’.**
 
• According to the Newlands Octaves, the properties of **Lithium and Sodium** were found to be the same.

**The image shows a demonstration of the arrangement made by Newland.**

 [IMAGE: https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20230918104609/Newland-Law.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**There were the following** limitations** of the** Newland's Law of Octaves**

 
• It was found that the **Law of Octaves** was **applicable only up to calcium,** as after calcium every eighth element did not possess properties similar to that of the first.
 
• It was assumed by Newlands that only 56 elements existed in nature and no more elements would be discovered in the future. But, later on, **several new elements were discovered, whose properties did not fit into the Law of Octaves.**
 
• After the **discovery of the Noble gases**, the **Law of Octaves became irrelevant**. Thus, Newlands’ Law of Octaves worked well with** lighter elements only.**
